chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Hammad from Al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Halab (Al-Halabi) from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding the Muqatib.

He pays part of his manumission debt, so he said: 'The people used not to stipulate [conditions], but today they do stipulate, and the Muslims are bound by their conditions. If he stipulated upon him that if he becomes unable [to pay], he returns [to slavery], and if he did not stipulate upon him, he does not return.'

key_terms.المُكَاتَب: A slave who has contracted with his master to pay a specific sum for his freedom in installments.
key_terms.عِنْدَ شُرُوطِهِمْ: Bound by their conditions / adhering to their stipulations.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on conditions stipulated in a slave's contract of manumission if they fail to pay the remaining debt?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar underscores the Shia juristic principle of 'al-Muslimun 'ala shurutihim' (Muslims are bound by their conditions), validating contractual autonomy in mukatabah agreements. It highlights the historical evolution from early prohibitions to the acceptance of stipulating reversion to slavery upon default, reflecting the pragmatic development of fiqh in managing debt and servitude. The ruling emphasizes that the master's explicit condition is the decisive factor in determining the slave's status upon inability to pay.
